title: Bonded Title vs. Salvage and Rebuilt Titles
excerpt: They get confused constantly and they describe different things. A bonded title is about missing paperwork. A salvage title is about the condition of the vehicle.
metaDescription: The difference between bonded, salvage and rebuilt titles: what each one means, what it does to resale value, and whether a vehicle can carry more than one.

body.text: These three get treated as interchangeable and they are not related. A bonded title is about missing paperwork. A salvage or rebuilt title is about what happened to the vehicle. A car can carry both at once, and confusing them costs people money on both sides of a sale.

rows: Ownership is backed by a surety bond because the original title is missing
Paperwork: a lost, never-delivered or defective title
An insurer declared the vehicle a total loss
Damage: collision, flood, fire or theft recovery
A salvage vehicle has been repaired and passed state inspection

body.text: A bonded title says nothing whatsoever about the condition of the vehicle. A salvage title says nothing about whether the paperwork is in order, which is a separate problem covered in [what is a defective vehicle title](/what-is-a-defective-vehicle-title).

Yes, and it is not unusual. A car totalled by an insurer, sold at auction without paperwork, then rebuilt, can end up needing a bonded title while also carrying a salvage or rebuilt brand. The bond resolves the ownership question. The brand stays, because the brand describes history that actually happened.

That is the key difference in how they behave over time. A bonded notation drops away when the bond term ends. A salvage or rebuilt brand follows the vehicle permanently, and the [national title record](https://vehiclehistory.bja.ojp.gov/) is designed precisely so that it cannot be washed away by moving the vehicle between states.

items: A bonded title has little lasting effect. The notation expires and buyers who understand it treat the vehicle as ordinary.
A salvage or rebuilt brand has a large and permanent effect, and also affects insurability and financing.
A buyer who confuses the two will discount a bonded title as though it were branded. That is worth correcting in the sale.

body.text: When neither is the right tool

If the dispute is over who owns the vehicle rather than over missing paperwork, a bond may not resolve it. A contested claim is a matter for a court, through a [quiet title action](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/quiet_title) or similar, not for a surety.

If your situation is the paperwork one, [what is a bonded title](/what-is-a-bonded-title) covers how it works and [what happens when your bonded title expires](/what-happens-when-your-bonded-title-expires) covers the end of the term.
